_why_two_claims: AGREEMENT asks whether the engines compute the same thing; RECOVERY asks whether they compute the right thing. Neither implies the other.

agreement.claim: both engines report the same proportion and the same Wilson and Clopper-Pearson bounds
agreement._note: Observed spread on the committed fixture: 0 at ten decimals on every key. The bounds are the point: R's binom and base binom.test against statsmodels' proportion_confint are independent implementations. harness/descriptive_examples.test.py also checks both against the closed-form Wilson and the beta-quantile Clopper-Pearson, and shows the Wald lower bound differs from Wilson's by 0.0035 on this fixture, far above the tolerance, so a silent fall-back to Wald fails.

recovery.claim: the estimated proportion is close to the one the fixture was built with

calibration.limits: Measured by harness/descriptive_examples.test.py over seeds 0 to 99 of this generator. It characterizes this synthetic generator, not every dataset. The committed fixture misses by 0.0125.
